info.name: Steward — Household Daemons
info.description:
Everything testable in this project: the three Swiggy Builders Club MCP servers (Food/Instamart/Dineout) via raw JSON-RPC, the manual PKCE OAuth flow that authenticates against them, the Steward web app's own routes, and the Telegram quick-add bot.

Import the companion Steward.postman_environment.json and select it before running anything -- request URLs/tokens are all environment variables, nothing is hardcoded.

Generated from this repo's own documented + live-verified findings (CLAUDE.md, DECISIONS.md, swiggy-mcp-reference.md) as of 2026-08-27 -- re-run tools/list before trusting exact tool counts, they've been wrong before (see the Instamart/Dineout folder descriptions for the two unresolved discrepancies).

item.name: Swiggy MCP
item.description: The three Builders Club MCP servers, plus the manual OAuth flow that authenticates against them. Confirmed live: this project has always called the production-shaped mcp.swiggy.com URLs, never mcp-staging.swiggy.com -- see CLAUDE.md's 2026-08-26 entry.

item.name: OAuth (manual PKCE)
item.description: Swiggy's authorization-server metadata has a known issuer/location mismatch (RFC 8414 §3.3) that breaks spec-strict discovery -- this is why the whole flow is manual here instead of an SDK's OAuthClientProvider. Generate a code_verifier/code_challenge (S256) yourself before running these (Postman doesn't do PKCE generation natively) and set oauth_code_verifier/oauth_code_challenge in the environment.

request.description: Returns a client_id. Copy it into the oauth_client_id environment variable.

item.name: 2. Authorize (open in a real browser, not Postman)

request.description: Postman can't complete phone+OTP login -- open this URL in an actual browser tab. The redirect will fail to load (nothing's listening on oauth_redirect_uri) -- copy the `code` query param from the resulting URL into oauth_authorization_code.

Returns a Bearer access token, 5-day expiry. Confirmed this session: no refresh_token is issued despite the auth server's metadata listing refresh_token as a supported grant type -- see DECISIONS.md 2026-08-24. Copy the access_token into swiggy_food_token / swiggy_im_token / swiggy_dineout_token as needed (same token works across all three servers).
Declares its authorization_servers as https://mcp.swiggy.com/auth.

item.name: [Known bug] Authorization-server metadata (served at root, not /auth)

request.description: This is the actual location the metadata is served from, but its own `issuer` field claims https://mcp.swiggy.com/auth -- a location/issuer mismatch per RFC 8414 §3.3. This is why spec-strict clients (MCP Inspector) refuse to connect with "Issuer mismatch". Worth re-checking periodically in case Swiggy fixes it.

item.name: Food server (20 tools)
item.description: https://mcp.swiggy.com/food. Tool count confirmed live at 20 (the reference doc claims 18 and omits create_address/delete_address -- CLAUDE.md's tool-inventory section). Response envelope shapes vary per tool -- get_food_cart's real total is nested at structuredContent.data.pricing.to_pay, deeper than any other tool; see CLAUDE.md before assuming a shape.

request.description: Always run this first against a fresh token -- tool inventories in the docs have been wrong before (see CLAUDE.md's spot-check log). This is the authoritative source, not the reference doc.
Note the field names: cartItems (not items), menu_item_id (not itemId) -- confirmed live, differs from the reference doc's guess.

MUTATING -- places a real order (sandbox: stubbed, ₹1000 cap, no real kitchen dispatch per CLAUDE.md). Real schema is much larger -- see swiggy-mcp-reference.md §6 for the full template before using this for anything but a smoke test. Not idempotent -- verify via get_food_orders on ambiguous response, don't retry blindly.
Widget-only poller -- returns epoch timestamps/cadence hints, not readable text. Use track_food_order for anything conversational.
Confirmed live this session: returns real delivered-order history, not just active orders as the reference doc's one-line description implies.
Paginates -- structuredContent.pagination.{page,pageSize,total,totalPages,hasMore}. Shared with Instamart; Dineout uses a separate get_saved_locations.
Not in the reference doc's Food table at all -- confirmed live to exist (CLAUDE.md's tool-inventory spot-check).
DESTRUCTIVE -- deletes a real saved address. Double-check address_id before running.

item.name: Instamart server (doc: 19 tools -- live count was 16, unresolved)
item.description: https://mcp.swiggy.com/im. The reference doc lists 19 tools; a live tools/list call earlier this session returned 16 and the full list wasn't captured at the time -- treat every tool below as unconfirmed until you re-run tools/list yourself. list_coupons/apply_coupon are GATED (whitelisted accounts only per the doc).

request.description: Always run this first against a fresh token -- tool inventories in the docs have been wrong before (see CLAUDE.md's spot-check log). This is the authoritative source, not the reference doc.
Returns products WITH variants (pack sizes/quantities) -- you need the spinId+skuId from a variation before update_cart.
Confirmed live this session: real, populated data -- frequently/recently ordered items. Closest thing to a pantry signal.
DESTRUCTIVE.
REPLACES the entire cart with the items given -- not an append. Read-merge-write if you want to add to an existing cart.
Real total lives at structuredContent.data.pricing / cartTotalAmount -- check the actual shape, don't assume.
GATED -- whitelisted accounts only.
GATED -- whitelisted accounts only.

MUTATING -- places AND confirms the grocery order in one call. ₹1000 sandbox cap. Never fall back to a proxy/guessed cart total when this drives a spend decision -- throw instead (see CLAUDE.md's 2026-08-26 hard-rule entry, born from a real ₹0-vs-real-total near miss).
Widget-only poller, same caveat as Food's get_food_delivery_status.
Confirmed live this session: works with NO required args, defaults to a 15-day lookback window. Returns real order history + preferences.

item.name: Dineout server (doc: 11 tools -- only 10 documented, gap unresolved)
item.description: https://mcp.swiggy.com/dineout. FREE reservations only (isFree=true, bookingPrice=0) -- book_table rejects paid deals. Address ID space is NOT separate from Food/Instamart despite the reference doc's claim -- get_saved_locations returned the identical home-address ID as Food's get_addresses in this session's testing (see DECISIONS.md 2026-08-25).

request.description: Always run this first against a fresh token -- tool inventories in the docs have been wrong before (see CLAUDE.md's spot-check log). This is the authoritative source, not the reference doc.

Confirmed live this session: accepts addressId OR raw latitude/longitude directly -- does not geocode area names itself. structuredContent is empty; real data is text-only in content[0].text (numbered list + "Search coordinates: latitude=..., longitude=...").
Looks up to 7 days ahead. Real slot data lives under _meta.slots, NOT structuredContent -- confirmed live, a fourth distinct envelope shape. Takes latitude/longitude directly, not addressId.
Validates billToPay=0 and skipPayment for free bookings.
MUTATING -- books a real (free) table. See DECISIONS.md's 2026-08-25 Dineout-verification entry for the full corrected schema before using this for more than a smoke test.
Paid-reservation UPI stage -- N/A for free bookings.
Restaurant name, date, time, guests, deal title, status.
UNCONFIRMED for Dineout specifically -- present on both Food and Instamart per the doc, but the Dineout table's 8 documented rows didn't show it. Run tools/list to check before relying on this.

item.name: Steward web app
item.description: Requires `npm run web` running locally (default http://localhost:3000). All mutating routes here go through the real Action Gate / world-model code -- nothing here is a mock.

item.name: Dashboard & actions
item.description: Server-rendered HTML, no JSON API -- these return full pages. Useful for smoke-testing the app is up and routes don't 500.

item.name: Telegram Bot API
item.description: The Standing Plans quick-add bot (src/telegram/). Runs long-polling (npm run telegram-bot), so getWebhookInfo should always show no webhook set -- if one appears, getUpdates will stop receiving messages until it's deleted.

request.description: Sanity check the token is valid.
Careful running this manually while the bot process is also polling -- Telegram only delivers each update once; concurrent getUpdates calls race on the offset.
Simulates what a user typing into the bot sends -- useful for testing parse-commitment.ts's extraction without needing to type on a phone.
